thread:
incident-bot: PAGERS -> KV_CACHE_HIGH_MISS: KV cache miss rate > 65% for inference-runtime-prod (us-west1) across multiple backends. Latency spike observed. Auto-page oncall

samira: I’m getting paged, jumping in. seeing retries and 500s in the dashboard. Is there a deploy around 10m ago?

alex: I rolled a batch-config tweak ~12m ago: lowered `batch.max_tokens` and increased `batch.concurrent` to try to reduce latency for short requests.

ricardo: that config change matches the spike start. miss rates on KV cache jumped right after. suspect continuous batching + hotter concurrency causing cache churn.

emily: HPA is reacting too. Observing rapid scaling events: scale up -> cache warming -> cache eviction -> miss spike -> scale up again -> thrash.

samira: customer impact? any >SEV1 tenants?

alex: host-metrics shows 3 tenants with elevated error rates; two are medium traffic (prod) customers. Not full outage but elevated tails and some rate limited client retries.

jonathan: ops: temporarily set manual HPA min replicas to stable value? We need to stop thrash while we investigate.

emily: agreed. applying a short-term HPA cap. Running: `kubectl patch hpa inference-runtime -n prod -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10, "maxReplicas":20}}'`

samira: do it and annotate with incident id. Also can we pin deployments to previous batch-config? rollback candidate.

alex: I can revert the batch-config change in config-service. Patch I applied is `batch.concurrent=16` -> revert to 8. Pushing now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by alex: config-service/batch-config:v2026.02. Refs: rollback -> batch.concurrent 8.

ricardo: while rollback is in progress, we should throttle new warmup traffic. Suggest enabling warmup hysteresis to avoid repeated prefix eviction.

emily: adding a temporary KV cache TTL bump and increasing allowed KV size limit so we don't evict during warmup. `kvctl set global.ttl 600` and `kvctl set cache.size_limit 30GB` (testing patch).

samira: good. also set a brief cooldown on the autoscaler to 5m to stop quick ramping.

alex: rollback completed. monitoring logs for miss-rate.

emily: miss rate dropping in telemetry, error rates for the two tenants trending down. HPA stabilized after cooldown applied.

samira: thanks. what's root cause summary for postmortem?

ricardo: summary draft: bad interaction between aggressive concurrent batching and our KV cache warmup behavior. High concurrency produced many interleaved prefixes, creating cache churn. With HPA reactively scaling, healthy pods got evicted or started without warmed caches -> higher miss rate -> more load on upstream -> autoscaler thrash.

alex: mitigation we applied: immediate rollback of batch.concurrent, temporary HPA min/max and cooldown, increase KV TTL/size, enable warmup hysteresis.

jonathan: recommend follow-ups: metric gated rollout for batching config (canary %), add a warmup health probe that counts cache-hit ratio before sending 100% traffic, and add autoscaler stabilization window tuned for cache-heavy workloads.

samira: assign action items: Alex -> create canary rollout PR + add telemetry gate (ETA today). Ricardo -> postmortem draft + add replayable test harness to simulate concurrent short-batch traffic (ETA tomorrow). Emily -> tune autoscaler defaults for cache-backed services and add runbook steps to throttle HPA (ETA EOD). Jonathan -> customer comms for the two affected tenants (I'll help).

alex: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/config-service/pull/487 - includes gating and config validation.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete for rollback, verifications passed.

emily: rechecked for 20m, no thrash and miss_rate stable ~3%. Looks green.

samira: closing pager for now. leaving this thread for handoff to postmortem. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Pager closed: KV_CACHE_HIGH_MISS. Duration: 00:38:46.

samira: adding notes to incident tracker and will start postmortem template. ping me if you saw any anomalies in the logs I missed.

ricardo: adding initial timeline to doc and attaching flame graphs.

alex: logging the exact config diff and adding test cases for concurrency matrix.

emily: will schedule a short playbook review on warmup/autoscaler next week.

jonathan: customer comms draft sent to legal and acct teams, prepping for any follow-ups.

samira: OK handoff complete — follow-ups captured. Keep thread updated if anything regresses.
